claims.text: Replacing EAM references with a machine-learning many-body potential trained on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations will substantially improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to solid and liquid multicomponent HEAs containing at least five principal metallic elements in near-equiatomic ratios.
The targeted temperature regime is at or above 0.9 times the alloy melting temperature.
The reference potential will be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations from both near-melting liquids and high-temperature solids.
The intended composition range comprises equiatomic or near-equiatomic 3d transition-metal HEAs.
A many-body machine-learning potential can represent local atomic environments in near-melting liquid and high-temperature solid phases more flexibly than a conventional EAM potential.
Multicomponent HEAs contain diverse local atomic environments that conventional EAM references may fail to capture.
Training the reference to reproduce ab initio forces and energies in relevant near-melting configurations will enable it to sample a broader range of local coordination environments than EAM.
Sampling a broader range of local coordination environments will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target overlap will reduce systematic errors along thermodynamic-integration paths.
The new reference will reduce free-energy path-integration discrepancies by at least a factor of two relative to EAM for solid–liquid transitions near melting.
Existing TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references for high-temperature multicomponent liquids often suffer from path-integration mismatch.
Successful application requires enough high-quality ab initio data to cover the relevant compositions and temperatures near melting.
The method is most directly applicable to 3d transition-metal-based HEAs with stable or metastable solid and liquid phases in the targeted temperature regime.
Failure of the fitted model to generalize beyond its training data may prevent improvement in reference–target overlap.
Omission of important high-temperature atomic interactions may limit the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path errors.
The hypothesis is falsified if the many-body reference fails to reduce the path-integration discrepancy by at least a factor of two relative to EAM when both are bridged to the same ab initio target.
